subject: react
summary: Explains React re-render conditions (state change, parent re-render, context change), React.memo shallow comparison, useMemo/useCallback memoization, and a measure-first optimization workflow.
key_points: React re-renders on state change, parent re-render, or context change — even when Props haven't changed.
React.memo skips re-render when Props are shallowly equal; inline object literals defeat this optimization.
useCallback is only effective when the child component is wrapped in React.memo — otherwise the child re-renders regardless.
misconceptions: useCallback alone prevents child re-renders without React.memo.
Every component should be wrapped in React.memo for better performance.
useMemo and useCallback have no cost — they are always beneficial.
check_questions: What are the three conditions that trigger a React component re-render?
Why does passing an inline object literal defeat React.memo?
When is it appropriate to add React.memo to a component?

fact_candidates: Three re-render triggers: state change, parent re-render, context change
React.memo uses shallow equality (===) to compare Props
practical_judgment_candidates: Deciding whether React.memo is warranted for a given component
Evaluating if useMemo/useCallback adds value vs. unnecessary complexity
error_interpretation_candidates: React.memo not preventing re-renders due to inline object Props
useCallback without React.memo having no performance benefit
scenario_candidates: Large table where only one row changes — memo + useCallback prevents 99 unnecessary re-renders
Dashboard with useMemo preventing expensive chart data recomputation on unrelated state change
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Believing useCallback alone stops child re-renders without React.memo
Assuming React.memo should be applied universally to all components
